memory_update.text: BWXT should remain the reference anchor for advanced nuclear components, fuel/fuel-handling, and naval nuclear propulsion exposure, but its size and visibility make it less suitable as the main underfollowed discovery candidate.

LEU is the strongest underfollowed public-market fuel-cycle chokepoint candidate for this node because HALEU licensing and production are regulated capacity constraints tied to many advanced-reactor designs.

CW is a second-order nuclear component supplier candidate: its nuclear exposure is embedded in a diversified industrial/defense portfolio, which may reduce theme purity but improve the 'hidden supplier' angle.

Need a follow-up search for smaller public suppliers of nuclear-grade valves, pumps, forgings, specialty alloys, inspection/NDE services, and machining where nuclear revenue is disclosed or inferable from qualified customer relationships.

Advanced fuel fabrication remains thinly investable in public markets: X-energy/TRISO-related fabrication appears private, BWXT is the public anchor, and LTBR is development-stage rather than scaled production.

node: Advanced nuclear components, reactor services, TRISO or advanced fuel fabrication, and naval/defense nuclear supply
summary: Expanded the node around regulated nuclear fuel, advanced fuel fabrication, reactor components, naval nuclear propulsion supply, and qualification-heavy nuclear hardware. The cleanest public-market chokepoint candidates are not speculative reactor developers but suppliers tied to HALEU enrichment, nuclear components, naval propulsion, and advanced fuel technology. This pass keeps BWXT as the reference anchor, elevates LEU and CW as investable supply-chain candidates, and adds LTBR only as a below-USD-300M speculative shadow because its relevance is fuel-technology optionality rather than proven scaled production.
